article.title: The Power of Active Recall
article.content: Many students spend hours rereading notes, but they remember little after a week. Active recall is different. Instead of looking at the answer, you try to pull information from memory. This effort strengthens neural connections and improves long-term retention. A simple way to practice is to close your notebook and explain the topic in your own words. If you get stuck, reopen the material, review briefly, and test yourself again. Over time, your brain learns that information must be ready for use, not just familiar on the page.
article.translation: 许多学生花很多时间反复看笔记，但一周后仍记不住多少内容。主动回忆则不同。你不是看答案，而是主动从记忆中提取信息。这种努力会强化神经连接，提升长期记忆。一个简单方法是合上笔记本，用自己的话讲解知识点。卡住时再短暂回看资料，然后继续自测。久而久之，大脑会学会把信息变成可调用的能力，而不是纸面上的熟悉感。

questions.prompt: What should you do when you get stuck?
options: Briefly review, then test yourself again
questions.explanation: 文中建议卡住时短暂回看材料，再继续自测。

questions.prompt: What is the intended result of this practice?
options: Information that is ready to use
questions.explanation: 最后一句强调信息应能随时调用，而不只是看起来熟悉。
